items.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
items.summary: The paper proposes viewing user embeddings as sparse combinations of interpretable behavioral modes to improve transparency in recommendation systems.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers a clearer, actionable understanding of user behavior for better model debugging and trust.

items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.summary: SwarmEvolve uses LLM-guided agent swarms to accelerate evolutionary search by refining and combining high-scoring solutions for computational problems.
items.whyItMatters: It speeds up AI-driven optimization, making complex problem solving more efficient for tech developers.

items.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
items.summary: The article introduces Scientist World, a platform that turns research papers into executable environments for AI scientists.
items.whyItMatters: It enables AI systems to run and test scientific ideas directly, accelerating automated research and discovery.

items.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
items.summary: XStack introduces a benchmark for migrating machine‑learning repositories between PyTorch/NVIDIA GPU and JAX/Google TPU ecosystems, enabling cross‑framework portability.
items.whyItMatters: It helps researchers unlock new hardware and improve reproducibility across popular ML frameworks.

items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.summary: The article examines when finite, noisy experiments can reliably identify causal mechanisms underlying integrated information in AI systems.
items.whyItMatters: It informs how to audit and interpret AI consciousness with limited data.

items.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
items.summary: The paper introduces MAEMs, models that map residual stream directions to text exemplars, enabling interpretation beyond corpus limits.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a scalable way to probe language model internals, aiding debugging and transparency for AI developers.

items.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
items.summary: The paper analyzes how large step sizes affect deterministic gradient descent dynamics in adversarial training, exploring implicit bias, optimization behavior, and loss sharpness.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding large-step effects can lead to faster, more robust training for real-world deep learning models.

items.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
items.summary: The article compares on‑policy distillation (OPD) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to assess compute efficiency across various tasks and model sizes.
items.whyItMatters: It informs whether OPD can cut training FLOPs while maintaining accuracy, a key concern for scalable AI development.

items.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
items.summary: ReproBridge proposes a system to capture and preserve detailed procedures and decisions from ML experiments, aiding reproducibility across papers, code, and artifacts.
items.whyItMatters: It helps researchers reliably replicate results, saving time and improving trust in AI research.

items.title: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions
items.summary: The paper proposes a Hidden Markov Preference Model to predict an attacker's next action, accounting for changing behavior regimes and time-varying action constraints.
items.whyItMatters: It offers defenders a dynamic, probabilistic tool to anticipate and counter evolving cyber threats more effectively.

items.title: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes
items.summary: The article examines how adding label wording variations improves a multilingual cross‑encoder’s accuracy on unfamiliar words but not on abbreviations or codes.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers should know that surface‑form augmentation can boost model robustness for new vocab, informing better prompt design.

items.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
items.summary: The article discusses mechanistic interpretability, exploring how to understand neural networks to ensure AI safety as they grow more autonomous.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because deeper insight reduces risks of unintended AI behavior.

items.title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
items.summary: LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes. We examine the errors of five memory systems on longitudinal medical dialogue and find three recurring causes: the retrieved evidence gives an outdated state, includes another person's health facts, or lacks a safety fact the answer depends on. items.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
items.summary: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. Yet the model sees the current dialogue but not the workspace around it. We explore meta access---giving the assistant a structured, permissioned view of the interface itself and propose a ladder of levels: feature tutoring; metadata, settings, and…

items.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods…

items.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
items.summary: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are…

items.title: On the limitations of molecular representations
items.summary: Molecular representations such as fingerprints and learned embeddings play a central role in cheminformatics and small-molecule machine learning. They serve as the primary input for a diverse array of tasks, including clustering, dataset splitting, and virtual screening, yet their evaluation is often limited to downstream model performance on narrow benchmark tasks. We carried out a systematic…

items.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
items.summary: Coding agents are among the most economically consequential deployments of LLMs to date, making reliable evaluation increasingly important. Yet even benchmarks that are carefully validated at release can become stale. As models improve, they can discover valid solutions that existing verifiers reject, while changes to evaluation infrastructure can invalidate assumptions embedded in tasks and…

items.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is commonly used in both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), often under similar optimizer settings. Yet, how the different dynamics of the two stages manifest in the low-rank increment that LoRA optimizes remains unclear. Tracking the singular spectrum and subspaces of LoRA updates on mathematical reasoning tasks, we find that RL concentrates…

items.title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?
items.summary: The growing use of AI in mathematics raises a question: can we detect AI involvement in proofs, separately from AI assistance with writing? Historical arXiv papers, recent papers disclosing substantive AI use, and manuscripts released by OpenAI provide a rich empirical basis for studying this question.
